report.summary: 4 findings survive review; high-severity item requires inspecting slice.py for missing 'included' list; medium items need bootstrap.py and containment.py checks; low item is theoretical. Plan orders by severity then cost.
risks: The 'included' list in slice.py may be missing, causing incorrect slice output when include_focus=False.
Catching BaseException in bootstrap.py may suppress SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt if not re-raised.
LowIntegrityLog.__init__ may not verify integrity label, leaving a gap in file-level attestation.
The fallback in _pick is theoretical and low risk.
todos: Open daedalus/structcore/slice.py and search for 'included' to verify list is updated.
Examine handler body in daedalus/spine/bootstrap.py lines 172-173 for exception handling.
Inspect LowIntegrityLog.__init__ in daedalus/spine/containment.py for integrity read-back.
Verify _spectrum never returns empty list for graphs with n>=3 and edges>0 (low priority).

items.title: Verify slice.py updates 'included' list when include_focus=False
items.why_now: Without this, the slice function may produce incorrect output (missing files in 'included' list), breaking the semantic slice contract and downstream tasks.

steps.do: Open daedalus/structcore/slice.py and search for 'included' variable. Check if it is updated when include_focus is False. If missing, add code to append focus_inc to included list when include_focus=False.
steps.verified_by: Write a test that calls semantic_slice with include_focus=False and asserts 'included' list contains the expected files (including focus_inc). Run `pytest tests/test_structcore_slice.py -x -v`.

items.assumption: The 'included' list is expected to be built in the slice function; if it already exists, this step becomes a no-op.

items.title: Inspect bootstrap.py except BaseException handler body
items.why_now: Catching BaseException without re-raising can suppress SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt, causing shutdown delays or improper cleanup.

steps.do: Open daedalus/spine/bootstrap.py and examine lines 172-173 (or the handler body after the except clause). If it does not re-raise SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt, add a check to re-raise those exceptions.
steps.verified_by: Write a test that mocks the refresh_sources function to raise KeyboardInterrupt and asserts it is not caught silently. Run `pytest tests/test_bootstrap_receipt.py -x -v`.

items.assumption: The handler body is in the same file; if it already re-raises, this step is a no-op.

items.title: Verify LowIntegrityLog.__init__ reads back integrity label
items.why_now: If the read-back is missing, the integrity label is not verified at file level, weakening the attestation chain.

steps.do: Open daedalus/spine/containment.py and inspect LowIntegrityLog.__init__ to see if it reads back the integrity label from the file and compares it to LOW_INTEGRITY_SID. If missing, add the read-back logic.
steps.verified_by: Write a test that creates a LowIntegrityLog, writes a label, and verifies that reading back matches. Run `pytest tests/test_containment.py -x -v`.

items.assumption: The LowIntegrityLog class is defined in containment.py; if it already verifies, this step is a no-op.

items.title: Verify _spectrum never returns empty list for valid graphs
items.why_now: Low severity, but confirming eliminates a theoretical fallback path and improves code clarity.

steps.do: Open daedalus/mapping/spectral.py and examine _spectrum function. Add a guard or comment that it never returns empty list for n>=3 and edges>0. Optionally add a unit test.
steps.verified_by: Write a test that calls _spectrum on a 3-node graph with 1 edge and asserts non-empty result. Run `pytest tests/test_mapping_spectral.py -x -v`.

items.assumption: The _spectrum function is in daedalus/mapping/spectral.py; if it already has a guard, this step becomes a documentation update.
